data_dictionary.none_state: NONE means the strategic base is destroyed or demolished and has not been rebuilt by either faction; it is effectively no-man's-land.
data_dictionary.rate_trends: Adjacent equal-window comparison. Array order is [recent_per_hour, previous_per_hour, change_per_hour, direction].
data_dictionary.recent_events: A direct ownership flip can produce a loss row plus a capture row for the same state transition.
data_dictionary.selected_metrics: Evidence citation keys whose values and observation times are frozen at prediction time.
data_dictionary.total_enlistments: Cumulative unique players who have deployed to this region during the war. A player can count in multiple regions. This is not current population or a faction split; its change is only a new-to-that-region activity proxy.

previous_model_summary.headline: Stlican Shelf Weathered Expanse Lead Heavy Fighting
previous_model_summary.war_summary: Since the 09:15 edition the front has tightened around a half‑dozen sectors. Stlican Shelf still records the highest turnover — four ownership changes in the last two hours and fifty‑four in the past day — though its one‑hour casualty rates are rising (colonial 7 /hr, warden 11 /hr) while the two‑hour trend shows both sides cooling. Weathered Expanse follows with three recent flips and sixty daily; colonial losses have slipped on the one‑hour window (‑71 /hr) but warden losses hold steady, and enlistments are easing. Callahan’s Passage has added four flips in two hours and twenty overall; casualties are cooling short‑term yet remain massive, and fresh enlistments are accelerating. Dead Lands has gone quiet in the last two hours but still logged sixteen daily flips; colonial casualties are accelerating (12 /hr) while warden casualties dip, with enlistments flat. Godcrofts shows no new flips in two hours but seventeen daily, modest casualties and a sharp rise in enlistments. Linn Mercy reports twelve daily events, no recent flips, and cooling casualties on both windows, though enlistments are picking up. The remaining regions remain largely inactive, with negligible events and stable, low casualty counts.
